title: Sprint-ready OKR Translator and Fallback Lane
creator: Maya Gonzalez
description:
Problem: Cross-functional teams frequently struggle to translate company-level OKRs into sprintable roadmap items while preserving capacity headroom and escalation paths. This leads to noisy prioritization meetings, hidden technical debt, and late-stage scope churn.

Goal: Ship a lightweight translator artifact and a "Fallback Lane" protocol that converts OKRs into 3 scenario-aligned roadmap slices (optimistic/core/conservative), ties each slice to capacity estimates and owner decision contracts, and defines automated fallback behavior when capacity or dependencies break. The deliverable will be a template, acceptance criteria, and a pilot with two initiatives in Q2.

Why this matters: Helps Product, Eng, Design, and GTM communicate deterministic trade-offs, reduces planning rework, and operationalizes contingency decisions so on-call and release owners can execute with fewer synchronous escalations.
proposal:
1) Build an "OKR Translator" template that maps each company OKR to: a) measurable outcome b) 3 roadmap slices (optimistic/core/conservative) c) slice-level acceptance criteria and SLO-like success gates d) capacity estimate (points/FTE-days) and e) primary/secondary owners and dependencies.

2) Define a Fallback Lane protocol: a compact contract that states what to disable, degrade, or postpone if capacity drops below the conservative slice. The fallback contract includes: automatic routing to lower-cost model variants, optional staggered rollouts, and an escalation path to the executive guardrail for SLAs.

3) Integrate into planning tooling: add fields to the roadmap intake form and generate a one-click summary for the quarterly planning review. Pilot with "Runtime Performance Playbook" and "Console Observability" initiatives.

4) Run a 6-week pilot, collect metrics and feedback, then iterate the template and embed into the initiative intake and release gating process.
acceptance_criteria: Translator template created and stored in Confluence with examples for two initiatives
Fallback Lane contract document approved by Eng, Product, Design and Security
Roadmap intake form updated and auto-generates a one-page OKR->slice summary
Pilot run for two initiatives with at least one scenario executed and documented
Stakeholder sign-off: PM lead, Eng manager, Design lead, and GTM owner

Week 2: Tooling changes (roadmap intake) scoped and PR opened
Week 3-4: Pilot initiative onboarding and execution
Week 5: Collect pilot telemetry and retro
Week 6: Finalize artifacts and handoff to Program Ops

Decision latency: median time to fallback decision < 4 hours during incidents
Coverage: 100% of company OKRs have a translator artifact by end of Q2
